tagline: Eleven farm miles on an old trail to the Mississippi.
intro: At Jewell the road crosses the Ogeechee River out of Hancock County and runs northeast on State Route 16, eleven miles over gently rolling hills, past farmland and a wildlife management area, into Warrenton.

It is the eastern end of the Historic Piedmont Scenic Byway, laid along a line that was once part of the Okfuskee Trail, the Native American path between the Augusta country and the Mississippi River. The Tour de Georgia bicycle race has come through twice.

moments.title: Jewell
moments.text: A settlement on the Ogeechee also known as Jewells Mills and Rock Factory, with its historic district just across the river in Hancock County.

moments.title: Beall Springs
moments.text: A community named for the Beall family, the first owners of the town site.

moments.title: Warrenton
moments.text: The county seat since 1797, where David Bushnell, builder of the first submarine used in battle, settled after the Revolution to teach at the academy, and died in 1824.
